passage:
The clock above the school office was always five minutes fast. Everyone knew this, but no one changed it.
Students liked the clock because it made them feel less late. Teachers joked that it helped everyone move faster.
One day, a new office worker fixed the clock. The next morning, several students arrived later than usual because they had trusted the old mistake.
The principal decided to keep the clock correct. He said, "A wrong clock may feel helpful, but it teaches the wrong habit."
Students complained for a few days. Then they got used to the correct time.
The clock did not change their lives greatly, but it reminded them that comfort and correctness are not always the same thing.
